# Job Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 421r

---

**14:1** "Man [adam] born of-woman [yelud ishah], short [qetser] of-days [yamim] and-full [useva] of-turmoil [rogez].

**14:2** Like-a-flower [ke-tsits] he-comes-out [yatsa] and-is-cut-down [vayyimmal]; and-he-flees [vayyivrach] like-the-shadow [katsel] and-does-not stand [velo ya'amod].

**14:3** Even upon this-one you-open [paqachta] your-eyes [einekha], and-me you-bring [tavi] into-judgment [bemishpat] with-you?

**14:4** Who can-bring [yitten] a-clean-thing [tahor] from an-unclean [mitame]? Not one [lo echad].

**14:5** If [im] his-days [yamav] [are] determined [charutsim], the-number [mispar] of-his-months [chodashav] [are] with-you; his-limit [chuqqo] you-have-made [asita], and-he-will-not pass-over [velo ya'avor].

**14:6** Look-away [she'eh] from-him and-let-him-rest [vechadal], until he-takes-pleasure-in [yirtseh] his-day like-a-hired-worker [ke-sakhir].

**14:7** For there-is [yesh] for-a-tree [la-ets] hope [tiqvah]: if it-is-cut-down [yikaret] yet-again [ve-od] it-will-sprout [yachalif], and-its-shoot [veyonaqto] will-not cease [lo techdal]. **14:8** If its-root [shorsho] grows-old [yazqin] in-the-earth [ba-arets], and-in-the-dust [be-afar] its-stump [giz'o] dies, **14:9** from-the-scent [me-reiach] of-water it-will-bud [yafriach], and-it-will-make [ve-asah] branches [qatsir] like-a-planting [kemo nata'].

**14:10** But-a-man [gever] dies and-lies-prostrate [vayechelash]; and-a-man [adam] expires [vayigva] and-where [ve-ayyo] [is] he?

**14:11** Waters [mayim] go [azelu] from-a-lake [mi-yam], and-a-river [venahar] dries-up [yecherav] and-becomes-dry [veyavesh]. **14:12** And-a-man [ve-ish] lies-down [shakhav] and-does-not rise [velo yaqum]; until [ad] no-more [bilti] [of the] heavens [shamayim] they-will-not awake [lo yaqitsu], and-they-will-not be-roused [velo ye'oru] from-their-sleep [mi-shenatam].

**14:13** Who-will-grant [mi yitten] [that] in-Sheol [bishe'ol] you-would-hide-me [tastireni], you-would-conceal-me [titspeneni] until [ad] turns [shuv] your-anger [appekha]; you-would-set [tashit] for-me a-limit [choq] and-remember-me [vetizkereni].

**14:14** If a-man [gever] dies, will-he-live [hayichyeh]? All the-days of-my-service [tseva'i] I-will-wait [ayachel], until my-renewal [chalifati] comes [bo].

**14:15** You-will-call [tiqra] and-I will-answer-you [va'aneka]; for-the-work of-your-hands [le-ma'aseh yadekha] you-will-long [tikhsof].

**14:16** For now my-steps [tse'adai] you-number [tisfor]; will-you-not [lo] keep-watch [tishmor] over my-sin [chatati]?

**14:17** Sealed-up [chatum] in-a-bag [bitsror] [is] my-transgression [pish'i], and-you-plaster-over [vatitpol] my-iniquity [avoni].

**14:18** But-indeed [ve-ulam] a-mountain [har] falling [nophel] crumbles [yibol], and-a-rock [tsur] is-removed [ye'teq] from-its-place [mimqomo]. **14:19** Stones [avanim] [the] waters [mayim] wear-away [shachaku]; its-overflows [seficheha] wash-away [tishtofe] the-dust [afar] of-the-earth [erets] — and-the-hope [vetiqvat] of-man [enosh] you-destroy [he'evadta].

**14:20** You-overpower-him [titqefehu] forever [lanetsach] and-he-goes [vayyehalekh]; you-change [meshaneh] his-face [panav] and-you-send-him-away [vateshalehehu].

**14:21** His-sons [banav] are-honored [yikhbedu] and-he-does-not know [velo yeda]; or-they-are-brought-low [veyits'aru] and-he-does-not perceive [lo yavin] them.

**14:22** Only his-flesh [besaro] upon-him is-in-pain [yikh'av], and-his-soul [nafsho] upon-him mourns [te'eval]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "born of woman":** The phrase *yelud ishah* emphasizes human frailty through the mode of origin. To be "born of woman" is to be mortal, limited, and subject to decay — a phrase Jesus echoes in Matthew 11:11.

**v.7-9 — The tree metaphor:** A cut-down tree can sprout again from its stump at the mere scent of water. But a dead man (v.10) has no such renewal. The contrast is devastating: a tree has more hope than a human being.

**v.12 — "until no more of the heavens":** This phrase (*ad bilti shamayim*) means "until the heavens are no more" — effectively "never." Job is not affirming resurrection but denying it. The dead do not wake.

**v.13-15 — Sheol as refuge:** A remarkable turn — Job wishes God would hide him in Sheol (the underworld) temporarily, then remember him and call him back. This is not resurrection doctrine but a desperate fantasy born of suffering.

**v.14 — chalifati:** Often translated "relief" or "renewal." The root *chalaf* means "to pass on, change, renew." Job imagines a changing of his condition — a release from the watch of death.

*— EMET*
